title: The Crooked Ember
premise: Zephyrine Lockridge, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has spent years keeping quiet ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things while hiding her gift. When a dying courier presses a map of the thirteenth moon into her hands, she learns the covenant binding the living realm to the dead is unraveling, and that her guildmaster engineered its breaking to hoard magic for the living alone. Hunted by guild enforcers and guided by the stubborn ghost of the courier, Zephyrine must gather three covenant-keys carved from her own family's bones and choose between restoring the covenant—which demands her memory as payment—and destroying it, which would silence the dead forever. In the end she reforges the covenant with a third option: she gives up her loyalty to the guild rather than her memories, exposing her master's treachery and becoming the new Voice between realms, bound no longer by duty but by love for those she carries.
about_author: N. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging funeral customs across coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write quiet, bone-deep fantasy about people who keep secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. In the guildhouse at Grayharbor, Zephyrine carves a keepsake from a widow's father's finger-bone and hears his last words—a warning about the moon. She files it away, as always. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a woman fluent in the dead and mute among the living.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tideline
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A courier washes ashore, dying, and presses a map inked on moon-skin into her hands, whispering 'thirteen turns.' The guild's enforcers arrive minutes too late; Zephyrine lies for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration as invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, with the courier's ghost, Wren, narrating interludes. Hiding in the bone-cellars, Zephyrine deciphers the map: it charts the covenant-marks where the realms were stitched together—and shows one already torn. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into trust.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Master Corvane discovers her absence and responds not with punishment but warmth, revealing he has always known about her gift—and offering to teach her its true depth. Zephyrine nearly accepts. Emotional beat: the seductive comfort of belonging, poisoned by doubt.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: POV Wren (ghost). Wren guides Zephyrine to the first key hidden in her mother's grave-marker—carved by Zephyrine herself, years ago, without knowing. Corvane's enforcers burn the cemetery behind them. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the past literally pursuing her.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Seeking passage, Zephyrine trades a memory of her first love to a ferryman of the drowned. Wren rages at the price; Zephyrine insists some things are worth forgetting. Emotional beat: love against duty—the first real cost of the road.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Cornered at the second key, Zephyrine learns the truth: Corvane broke the covenant deliberately, believing the dead are parasites, and he offers her his vision of a living-only world—with her as its Voice. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: The Broken Stitch
chapters.summary: POV alternating Zephyrine/Wren. At the final covenant-mark, the veil tears open; the dead pour through, not as monsters but as the forgotten poor, begging to be remembered. Zephyrine holds the last key—her own knucklebone—and hesitates. Emotional beat: horror transfigured into compassion.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Climax. Confronting Corvane atop the mark, Zephyrine refuses both his world and the covenant's price. Instead she carves her loyalty to the guild out of herself and binds it into the new covenant, making truth—not obedience—its anchor. Corvane falls silent, unmade by his own broken oath. Emotional beat: sacrifice redefined.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, coda in Wren's voice. The moon completes its turn and passes whole. Zephyrine opens a small shop above the tideline, carving freely, hearing gladly, keeping a ledger of names instead of debts. Wren stays, choosing to linger. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted—memory kept, duty transformed into love.
